sentences.text: Its skull is elongated and platyrostral, featuring broadened nasals and a flattened innerfenestral bar.
The rectangular lacrimal bone is twice as long as it is wide.
A pitted ventral region on the quadratojugal bone creates a characteristic indentation.
The genus name refers to the animal's doubly pierced palate.
A crest on its back scales suggests muscles attached differently than in modern crocodilians.
The holotype specimen was discovered by Edwin Delfs in 1957 in the Morrison Formation near Canon City, Colorado.
Charles Mook first described the species in detail in 1967.
The species name delfsi honors the discoverer Edwin Delfs.
The fossil record includes an almost-complete skull and some limb bones.
Specimens are estimated to have weighed between 50 and 60 kg.
Evidence suggests it was carnivorous, feeding on insects, fish, small reptiles, mammals, and dinosaurs.
Chemical analysis of its teeth suggests a diet focused on fish.
It is categorized as a semi-aquatic animal.
Eutretauranosuchus delfsi is the only known species in the genus.
Related genera include Amphicotylus, Goniopholis, Sunosuchus, and Calsoyasuchus.
Fossils are found in the Morrison Formation in Colorado and Wyoming.
It lived in estuarine and freshwater environments.
It lived between 154.8 and 143.1 million years ago.
Recent research suggests the additional nasal opening described by Mook was an illusion caused by an hourglass-shaped choana.
Some analyses place it closer to Pholidosaurus and dyrosaurids within a larger clade including Bernissartia and eusuchians.
